Blood cells are formed from tissue stem cells in the bone marrow. These bone marrow stem cells go through a number of mitotic cell cycles to form the fully functioning blood cell.

Fig. 5.1 shows the three main stages of the cell cycle.

{{figure:figure_5_1.webp}}

Fig. 5.1

The activity of genes changes during the mitotic cell cycle.

When genes are being expressed, the cell produces many messenger RNA (mRNA) molecules and ATP molecules.
